messages.subject: closed landmark curves
parts:
Hi all,

I'm looking for advice on how to handle outlines using GM - for example outlines of butterfly wings. If this could be described by a "closed" curve (so, no anatomical landmarks but using Type 3 landmarks with equal spacing), is the potential issue with alignment solved by sliding during the GPA or are there other steps that should be considered? 

From what I remember from the geomorph workshop, one uses an iterative process of sliding & GPA to minimise the Procrustes distance to the consensus shape, but in practice I don't know how that is done.

Any tips or relative literature would be appreciated!

Thanks,
Christy

messages.author: 635bd93e270bc751
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] closed landmark curves
parts:
Hi Christy

While this is in many ways off-topic, in that I didn’t use closed curves, nor, for that matter, did I use geomorph R, I did grapple with the shape of butterfly wings (and also claws) in my PhD. If you can face wading through it, you might find something helpful in my methodology, using Type 1 landmarks. There are bibliographies at the end of each chapter which might provide helpful pointers.

You can find it on http://eprints.bournemouth.ac.uk/34977/

Best wishes

Nigel

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] closed landmark curves
parts:
Christy,

 

GPA with sliding is:

 

Translation, scale, rotation, slide. Find mean shape, Iterate. It will work with all semilandmarks, though I find it a bit more stable with at least one fixed point. However, recall that the original 1997 paper introducing the approach used all sliding landmarks on the corpus callosum.

 

Dean
